newsitem.title: LEBANON: Seven Israeli soldiers wounded in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Seven Israeli soldiers wounded in Lebanon.

text.p: Seven Israeli soldiers were wounded on Sunday in south Lebanon in the bloodiest clash with pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas in more than a week, pro-Israeli militia sources said.
In retaliation Israeli jets rocketed suspected Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrilla targets in the area.

The South Lebanon Army (SLA) sources said the guerrillas first set off a bomb by an Israeli patrol near the Blat post in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone before firing machineguns and Sagger anti-tank rockets, scoring a direct hit on a tank.
They said other guerrillas fired mortar bombs into Blat, in the western sector of the zone meandering along the Lebanese side of the border from Mount Hermon to the Mediterranean.
Seven Israeli soldiers were wounded, the SLA sources added.
Sunday's attack was the bloodiest on the last active Arab-Israeli frontline since January 30 when three Israeli soldiers were killed in a Hizbollah bomb attack in the zone.
So far this year, four Israeli soldiers have been killed and 19 wounded in south Lebanon compared with 27 killed last year.

The combat casualties, coupled with the mid-air collision of two Lebanon-bound Israeli helicopters last week that killed 73 soldiers, has sparked a debate in Israel over its continued occupation of the south Lebanon border strip.

The casualties of the crash -- soldiers and officers bound to the south Lebanon zone -- exceeded by three the number of fatalities inflicted by Hizbollah in the past three years in its war against Israeli soldiers in the buffer strip.

An Israeli legislator, former Shin Bet secret service man Gideon Ezra, said on Sunday that a group of Israeli lawmakers and veteran security men want the Israeli government to reconsider policy in Lebanon after the helicopters' crash.
Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said after the Tuesday night crash that Israel should draw a lesson from the incident and end its occupation of south Lebanon.
But Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday said he rejects a unilateral Israeli withdrawal from the zone, saying it would bring Hizbollah "terrorists" closer to northern Israel.
He said Israel must stabilise its northern border before it could leave and that would be difficult without agreement from Syria, Israel's arch-foe and Lebanon's main power broker.

Former Israeli Prime Minsiter Shimon Peres -- who ordered a bloody 17-day blitz against Hizbollah in Lebanon last April but failed to crush the group -- has suggested after the crash speeding up peace negotiations with Beirut and Damascus.

In Beirut, Hizbollah claimed responsibility for Sunday's attack, saying in a statement its fighters ambushed an Israeli patrol of the elite Egoz unit after other fighters lured them to a "fake ambush". It said eight soldiers were killed or wounded.

"God has made the usurper Zionists taste the worst torture and annihilated them in mid-air so Moslems were overjoyed... Today, the Islamic Resistance completes the Moslems' joy on Eid al-Fitr (feast) with a new victory against the enemy," it said.
After the latest attack, Israeli jets hit twice near the village of Zibqine just north of the zone facing Blat, security sources said. Israeli gunners also shelled nearby areas.
There was no immediate word on casualties. Hizbollah said that its fighters fired SAM-7 missiles at the attacking jets.
Hizbollah is fighting to oust 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 allied SLA militia from the 15-km (nine-miles)-deep south Lebanon zone set up in 1985 to ward off raids on north Israel.
